recognition: Recognize the supplied source as the public UCI Appliances Energy Prediction dataset (UCI 374) and its listed 2017 Candanedo et al. paper. This recognition uses the supplied documentation; no remembered study result is being treated as evidence.
summary: Retain and sharpen I1 as a measurement-efficiency proposal. Because each aggregate Appliances value is a completed 10-minute interval, it cannot trigger circuit logging within that same interval. Define an event at interval t using a threshold learned only from the earlier calibration period, then start logging at t+1. Compare the equal-count trigger and week/hour-matched random schedules on held-out intervals. Existing rows can audit timing, event frequency, and aggregate-load enrichment only; circuit attribution requires synchronized circuit Wh labels.

candidates.title: Trigger temporary submeter logging after household load events
candidates.question: With the same number of logged 10-minute intervals, does starting circuit-submeter logging immediately after a high aggregate Appliances interval capture more subsequent high-use intervals with a dominant measured circuit than week- and hour-matched random logging?
candidates.new_claim: A two-stage monitoring policy may improve the yield of scarce circuit-level logging for characterizing persistent or recurring high-use episodes. This is a measurement-efficiency hypothesis, not a claim about reducing energy use.
candidates.input_delta: The supplied data has whole-home Appliances Wh per completed 10-minute interval but no circuit readings. Add a prospective comparison of logging in the interval after an aggregate-load trigger versus equal-count, calendar-week and hour-of-day-matched random intervals, with synchronized circuit Wh evaluation labels.
candidates.domain_value: A building-energy team could use limited temporary logger bandwidth to characterize circuits around recurring high-use episodes and prioritize later control or maintenance investigations.
assumptions: The whole-home meter reports each 10-minute interval soon enough to start circuit logging in the next interval.
Circuit meters can be synchronized to the whole-home meter, and the measured circuit Wh can be reconciled with aggregate Appliances Wh within a pre-specified tolerance.
Some high-use episodes persist or recur into the following interval; this is unverified.
A single-home pilot can establish feasibility and within-home utility only, not generalization across households.
variables_and_units: Aggregate Appliances energy, Wh per completed 10-minute interval
Circuit-level energy, Wh per synchronized 10-minute interval
Logging effort, number of logged intervals

High-use capture yield, number of logged held-out intervals above the frozen calibration threshold with a measured leading circuit contributing at least 50% of aggregate Appliances Wh, per 100 logging slots
Calendar week and hour of day, matching strata
candidates.testable_prediction: Set the event threshold to the 90th percentile of Appliances Wh in the first 60% of chronologically ordered rows, before examining held-out outcomes. In the held-out period, log the interval immediately after each threshold-crossing interval. At equal logging-slot count, week/hour-matched random schedules will have lower high-use capture yield than event-triggered schedules. The percentile, 50% circuit-share criterion, interval lag, and equal-budget rule are fixed prospectively here; the compute request audits only aggregate schedule feasibility and does not test attribution.
candidates.alternative: High loads may be brief, so they end before the next interval; alternatively, circuits may share load and no single circuit may contribute half. In either case, the event-trigger policy may have no higher circuit-attribution yield than matched random logging.
candidates.discriminating_test: In a prospective single-home pilot, collect synchronized whole-home and circuit-level Wh continuously as reference truth during a held-out evaluation period, while scoring two pre-registered logging schedules with equal numbers of 10-minute slots: (a) log interval t+1 when Appliances at t exceeds the 90th percentile fixed from the first 60% chronological calibration period, and (b) randomly choose the same number of slots matched within calendar week and hour of day. Define a successful slot as one where Appliances Wh is at or above the frozen threshold and the measured leading circuit contributes at least 50% of aggregate Appliances Wh. Compare successful slots per 100 logging slots; report paired week-level differences and uncertainty, and retain weeks with zero eligible slots in the accounting. Continuous reference truth is needed to score unlogged counterfactual slots during the pilot, so this first test establishes monitoring-policy value under validation instrumentation rather than immediate meter-cost savings.
candidates.feasible_with_current_data: Partly. Dates and aggregate Appliances Wh support a calibration-only trigger, next-interval timing audit, and aggregate high-use capture comparison. No circuit attribution, 50% share outcome, causal saving, or actual temporary-meter performance can be assessed.
candidates.required_new_data: For an initial home pilot, obtain synchronized whole-home Appliances Wh and circuit-level Wh for every 10-minute interval during calibration and held-out weeks, with meter reconciliation and schedule activation/logging flags. Continuous circuit measurements serve as reference truth for this test. Replicate across homes before claiming household-level generalization or cost savings.
candidates.failure_condition: The proposal's aggregate feasibility premise fails if the trigger produces too few held-out next-interval slots or does not enrich logged slots for above-threshold aggregate Wh compared with the matched random schedule. Its circuit-level prediction fails if, at equal logging-slot count, event-triggered logging does not increase successful slots per 100 slots over matched random logging, or if the gain is confined to isolated weeks. A single-home result cannot support a population claim.
candidates.nearest_prior_query: Crossref query: residential household event-triggered circuit submeter logging compared with equal-budget, time-matched random logging for identifying circuits contributing to persistent or recurring high-load intervals.

candidates.title: Use room thermal recovery traces to target ventilation checks
candidates.question: After comparable outdoor-temperature changes, do room-specific temperature recovery traces identify periods when measured ventilation or air exchange is unusually high, beyond the information in airport weather alone?
candidates.new_claim: A room-to-room thermal recovery signature could help schedule ventilation diagnostics, but only if it agrees with direct air-exchange measurement under controlled operating conditions.
candidates.input_delta: The file supplies 10-minute room temperatures T1-T9, north-side outdoor T6, airport T_out, and weather, but no ventilation, window, or HVAC-state labels. Add direct air-exchange measurements and logged operating states to test a diagnostic use of thermal response traces.
candidates.domain_value: A validated signature could prioritize building-envelope or ventilation checks when continuous airflow sensing is unavailable.
assumptions: Room temperature response contains a measurable ventilation-related component.
Heating, solar gains, occupancy, and sensor placement can be measured or controlled sufficiently to distinguish competing causes.
A single-house observational trace is hypothesis-generating only.
variables_and_units: Room and north-side temperatures T1-T9 and T6, degrees C per 10-minute interval
Airport outdoor temperature T_out, degrees C per 10-minute interval
Air-change rate, h^-1, measured by tracer-gas decay
Window/HVAC operating state, categorical with timestamps
candidates.testable_prediction: Within controlled, matched temperature-step trials, a pre-specified room-temperature recovery time will be shorter at higher directly measured air-change rates after accounting for logged HVAC and window states; the association should replicate across rooms or trial days.
candidates.alternative: Thermal mass, internal gains, or control cycling may dominate recovery time, leaving no stable relationship with measured air-change rate.
candidates.discriminating_test: Run repeated controlled trials in the same home with randomized window/ventilation settings, direct tracer-gas air-change measurements in h^-1, and synchronized 10-minute room/outdoor temperatures. Compare recovery-time slopes across settings within room and day; record HVAC state and reject trials with unmeasured operating changes. Use existing rows only to pre-specify candidate rooms and ranges, not as validation of ventilation.
candidates.feasible_with_current_data: Exploratory thermal traces are available, but validation against ventilation and separation from HVAC, occupancy, and solar gains are not feasible.
candidates.required_new_data: Repeated room-level tracer-gas air-change measurements in h^-1, window and HVAC state logs, and preferably occupancy/solar-gain proxies synchronized with room temperatures; replicate trials over multiple days and homes.
candidates.failure_condition: The proposed diagnostic fails if recovery time does not change consistently with directly measured air-change rate within controlled matched trials, or if HVAC/window state explains the apparent signature better than air exchange.
candidates.nearest_prior_query: Crossref query: residential room temperature decay or thermal recovery as an indicator of measured air change rate, validated with tracer gas under logged HVAC and window states.

candidates.title: Test occupancy-triggered feedback for flexible household loads
candidates.question: Does brief, privacy-preserving feedback after a high appliance-load interval reduce energy in the next hour without worsening indoor comfort, compared with the same feedback delivered at matched non-event times?
candidates.new_claim: A load-event-timed feedback intervention may shift flexible household appliance use; the timing effect is unknown and must be randomized rather than inferred from observational traces.
candidates.input_delta: The dataset has aggregate Appliances and lights Wh, room climate, and dates, but no occupancy, appliance identity, feedback, or comfort ratings. Add a randomized feedback intervention with those measurements.
candidates.domain_value: If effective and comfortable, an energy team could time low-cost prompts to moments when a household has a meaningful opportunity to defer flexible use.
assumptions: Some high-load intervals include deferrable use rather than fixed or essential loads.
A household can receive and act on a prompt.
A one-home trial estimates an individual response and cannot establish population effects.
variables_and_units: Appliance energy, Wh per 10-minute interval and summed Wh over the next 60 minutes
Prompt assignment and delivery time, binary and timestamp
Occupant comfort, pre-specified ordinal response scale
candidates.testable_prediction: Within-house randomized event-timed prompts will reduce next-hour appliance Wh relative to matched no-prompt event windows without increasing the pre-specified rate of comfort reports outside the acceptable range.
candidates.alternative: Loads may be non-deferrable, prompts may be ignored, or reductions may be rebound into the following hours; event timing may offer no advantage over ordinary prompts.
candidates.discriminating_test: After a baseline period, randomize eligible high-load events within household and time-of-day blocks to event-timed prompt or no prompt, and separately randomize matched non-event prompt windows if testing timing specificity. Measure whole-home appliance Wh continuously, occupancy only with consent, and comfort before and after the next hour. Pre-register the next-hour Wh contrast, rebound window, and comfort threshold.
candidates.feasible_with_current_data: No. The series describes energy and climate but contains no prompt, occupancy, or comfort data and is observational.
candidates.required_new_data: A consented randomized household pilot with prompt assignment/delivery logs, continuous appliance Wh, occupancy or response availability, and repeated comfort ratings; include several post-prompt hours to measure rebound.
candidates.failure_condition: The intervention fails if event-timed prompts do not reduce next-hour Wh relative to randomized controls, if the effect is offset by rebound within the pre-specified follow-up period, or if comfort worsens beyond the registered limit.
candidates.nearest_prior_query: Crossref query: randomized event-triggered residential energy feedback prompts versus time-matched prompts or control, measuring appliance energy, comfort, and rebound.

task.deliverable: Critique I1 and tighten it into a prospective monitoring-policy protocol that handles trigger latency, equal logging budgets, circuit attribution, and the correct replication unit. Separate aggregate schedule feasibility from circuit-level evidence.
acceptance: Retain or revise I1 with a concrete alternative and failure rule.

Fix the trigger to the 90th percentile of Appliances in the first 60% chronological calibration rows; trigger logging in the next interval because the current interval's aggregate is observed only after completion.
Compare equal-count logged slots with a random schedule matched by held-out calendar week and hour of day; define the result per 100 slots and report paired week-level uncertainty.
Define success using held-out aggregate Appliances at or above the frozen threshold plus a measured leading circuit contributing at least 50% of aggregate Appliances Wh.
State that the current file can assess aggregate schedule feasibility only, not circuit attribution, energy savings, or intervention effects.
task.proposed_computation: Using supplied DF only, parse dates, split chronologically at 60%, freeze the calibration 90th-percentile Appliances threshold, and audit the event-at-t then log-at-t+1 schedule on held-out rows. Report event-slot count, aggregate high-use share, and a descriptive week/hour-matched random schedule comparison at equal slot count. This checks whether the proposed schedule is temporally feasible and enriches aggregate high-use slots; it cannot test circuit attribution or savings.
task.proposed_search: A focused Crossref query can check for direct comparisons of event-triggered household circuit submeter logging with equal-budget, week/time-matched random logging and circuit-level attribution outcomes. A close match would narrow novelty to the one-interval-lag and the explicit per-slot dominant-circuit outcome; a title alone will not establish the prior study's result.

critique: The original wording implied that an interval's aggregate Wh could trigger circuit logging during that same interval. The meter reports an interval total after its end, so I revised the policy to trigger at t and begin logging at t+1. This changes the target to persistent or recurring high-use episodes; short events that do not persist are an explicit alternative.

The original 'more high-use energy' and 'leading circuit' outcome did not specify a denominator or distinguish a captured high-use slot from an attributable circuit. I define successful slots and yield per 100 slots, with aggregate and circuit labels both required.

An equal number of sampled intervals is the operational budget proxy, not a complete cost model. Continuous circuit reference measurements are needed to evaluate counterfactual schedules in an initial validation pilot; this does not itself show real deployment savings.

The 60/40 chronological split and 90th-percentile threshold are a pre-specified protocol choice for this proposal, not an evidence-derived optimum. One home's weeks are the available repeated units; rows must not be treated as independent households.

requests.purpose: Audit the aggregate-only premise that a frozen calibration threshold can produce next-interval trigger slots enriched for held-out above-threshold Appliances intervals, and check whether week/hour strata support an equal-count random comparison. This is descriptive feasibility only, not circuit attribution or causal evidence.
requests.model_spec: Chronologically sort supplied DF by parsed date. Use the first floor(0.60*n) rows as calibration and the remainder as held-out evaluation. Freeze threshold q90 of calibration Appliances. Define a held-out logging slot at t+1 when Appliances at t is at least that threshold. Compare trigger slots with repeated week/hour-matched random slots of equal count, and report compact JSON aggregate metrics. Do not infer independent household replication.
requests.code:
import json
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

d = DF[['date', 'Appliances']].copy()
d['ts'] = pd.to_datetime(d['date'], format='%Y-%m-%d%H:%M:%S')
d = d.sort_values('ts').reset_index(drop=True)
cut = int(len(d) * 0.60)
cal = d.iloc[:cut].copy()
test = d.iloc[cut:].copy()
threshold = float(cal['Appliances'].quantile(0.90))
d['trigger_next'] = d['Appliances'].shift(1).ge(threshold).fillna(False)
test['trigger'] = d.loc[test.index, 'trigger_next'].to_numpy()
test['high'] = test['Appliances'].ge(threshold)
test['week'] = test['ts'].dt.strftime('%G-%V')
test['hour'] = test['ts'].dt.hour
trigger = test[test['trigger']]
strata = [(key, len(g)) for key, g in trigger.groupby(['week', 'hour'], sort=True)]
rng = np.random.default_rng(20261102)
draw_means = []
matched_slots = 0
for key, n_slots in strata:
    pool_mask = (test['week'].eq(key[0]) & test['hour'].eq(key[1]))
    pool = test.loc[pool_mask]
    matched_slots += min(n_slots, len(pool))
for _ in range(200):
    chosen = []
    for key, n_slots in strata:
        pool_mask = (test['week'].eq(key[0]) & test['hour'].eq(key[1]))
        pool = test.loc[pool_mask]
        n = min(n_slots, len(pool))
        if n:
            chosen.extend(rng.choice(pool.index.to_numpy(), size=n, replace=False).tolist())
    sample = test.loc[chosen]
    draw_means.append(float(sample['high'].mean()) if len(sample) else None)
out = {
    'calibration_rows': int(len(cal)),
    'heldout_rows': int(len(test)),
    'threshold_wh_per_10min': threshold,
    'trigger_slots': int(len(trigger)),
    'trigger_high_share': float(trigger['high'].mean()) if len(trigger) else None,
    'matched_random_slots_per_draw': int(matched_slots),
    'matched_random_high_share_mean_200_draws': float(np.mean([x for x in draw_means if x is not None])) if any(x is not None for x in draw_means) else None,
    'random_draws': 200,
    'interpretation': 'Aggregate schedule feasibility only; no circuit labels or causal savings.'
}
print(json.dumps(out, separators=(',', ':')))

requests.query: Crossref search for residential household electricity event-triggered submetering or circuit logging compared with random or time-matched sampling, reporting appliance/circuit attribution or high-load event capture.
requests.change_if_found: A close direct comparison would make the idea a replication or protocol refinement rather than a broad new monitoring-policy claim; narrow the addition to the one-interval trigger latency and the registered dominant-circuit-per-slot outcome.
